analysis.title: Credit Market Outlook & Strategy: Hyper-ventilating again
key_insights: HG spreads are retesting recent wides, with JULI +4bp WoW to 96bp. Most of the move followed Wednesday's hot CPI print, which raised fears of faster Fed tightening and hit the areas most reliant on incremental debt (HY neoclouds and, by extension, HG hyperscalers).

Markets ended the week pricing the same odds of a Fed hike this month as at the start of the week (17%), and HG yields fell 22bp WTD. JPM says it would have been less constructive had yields spiked after CPI. Yields stabilizing near the highs supports returns and demand, so the bank stays constructive on HG spreads.

HG total returns rebounded to 1.3% MTD, recouping about half of September's -2.7%. The mutual fund universe just registered its largest outflow since April 2025, and JPM expects outflows to reverse as returns recover.

Supply is supportive. Net-net supply was negative for the last two weeks, and next week brings $36bn of coupons and maturities, 26% above the 2026 weekly average. The next catalyst is hyperscaler earnings (META and SPCX this week), since earnings releases marked the hyperscaler spread wides this past summer.

Hyperscaler spreads widened 12bp WoW to 148bp, the widest since July 2026 and 6bp off the YTD wide of 154bp. JULI sector-weighted dispersion rose to 21.2bp, the widest since May 2025. The BBB-A non-financial gap widened 3bp to 37bp, the widest since April 2026. Investors are demanding more compensation for lower-rated and capital-intensive credits rather than selling HG broadly.

JPM calls the hyperscaler widening overdone unless upcoming earnings show fundamental weakness. Despite a $117bn increase in hyperscaler debt YTD, the cohort's average rating improved (index ratings score 5.12 vs 5.18 at YE25) because the new debt came mainly from higher-rated Amazon, Alphabet and Meta. JPM sees front-end Financials as a defensive area likely to outperform.

Midterm elections: JPM concludes that political control is not a useful driver of HG spread positioning. A regression since 1954 shows Fed policy is statistically significant for spread changes (p=0.006, -3.15bp effect) while government control is not (p=0.411). Polling points to divided government as the most likely outcome. Sector effects flow through five channels: fiscal and Treasury supply, regulation and M&A, trade policy, consumer affordability and AI infrastructure.

3Q26 ratings: $85bn of debt was re-rated, down from $270bn in 2Q26. Upgrades were $64bn and downgrades $21bn, a 3.1x ratio. The YTD upgrade/downgrade ratio is 2.3x versus 1.9x in 2025. The BBB share of JULI fell to 42.8%, the lowest since 2Q12. Rising Stars exceeded Fallen Angels for the first time this year ($9bn vs $5bn).

Fallen Angel pipeline: $654bn of BBB- debt, with $171bn one notch from HY. BBB- debt with both an HY rating and a negative outlook is $44bn, mostly Ford ($42bn). JPM expects $25bn of Rising Stars ($96bn total) against $72bn of Fallen Angels ($144bn total) in 2026/27.

New issue performance had its worst week since April 2020: new issues were 25bp wider versus the index 2bp tighter, a 27bp gap, tied to the PSKY/SKYD new issue. Excluding those bonds, the remaining $15bn cohort outperformed by about 4bp. This is the second >5bp underperformance episode this year, and primary volume tends to fall about 32% after such episodes.

USD French banks: the USD HG French bank index is 21bp wider over the month to 137bp, the widest since May 2025, with a 44bp discount to other Yankee banks. JPM's model puts fair value at 114bp, so the bonds trade 23bp wide of fair value. The 10y OAT-Bund spread is 138.5bp. JPM views the risk as appropriately priced and starting to look slightly cheap, but sees no rally before progress on French budget negotiations.

Issuance is concentrating. There were 604 unique HG issuers YTD, 16% below FY2025. The top 25 issuers raised a record $587bn (34.6% of supply vs 26.0% in 2025). Core AI (+$217bn) and banks (+$119bn) explain 86% of the $391bn y/y increase. 'Physical economy' issuers are stepping back, with supply down 26% y/y. JPM calls rising concentration a long-term negative if it persists.

September HG issuance was $197bn (+33% vs the four-year September average), and YTD supply is $1.69tr (+30% y/y), 85% of the $2.0tr full-year forecast. M&A-related issuance hit $61bn in September, the highest monthly total of 2026, and YTD M&A funding is $252bn. The long-end share of issuance fell to 12.4% and the average new-issue coupon was 5.63%, the highest since April 2024.

Fund flows: HG inflows stalled to $1.9bn (-82% WoW). Mutual funds saw $4.8bn of outflows, of which $2.1bn came from a single foreign fund, while ETFs took in $6.7bn. HY funds lost $1.3bn and muni inflows of $4.5bn were the largest since at least September 2007.

Hyperscaler monitor: JULI is 96.4bp, ex-hyperscalers 92.8bp and hyperscalers 147.8bp (+11.8bp WoW, +43.5bp YTD). ORCL (+37bp WoW) contributed 6.2bp of the move. Hyperscalers are 4.7% of JULI by par and 3.7bp of its spread.

Foreign demand: the FAB index fell 5bp WoW to 63bp. Forward markets price about a 20% chance of a Fed hike in October. JPM's economics view is that those odds fall to zero after the next CPI. Overnight net buying rose 25% WoW to $300mn/night.
Curves are at the midpoint of their 1y ranges: 3s5s at 16bp, 5s10s at 24bp, 10s30s at 17bp. The hyperscaler 10s30s curve is much steeper at 46bp versus 13bp ex-hyperscalers.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM says the widening looks overdone: the cohort's average rating improved despite a $117bn debt increase YTD, and yields stabilizing near highs supports demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors are weighing AI funding needs, prospective supply and weaker AI equity performance. Hyperscaler spreads are 6bp off YTD wides and dispersion is at multi-year highs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upcoming hyperscaler earnings (META and SPCX this week) revealing fundamental weakness, or yields spiking higher after CPI.

tension_points.bull_case: Bonds trade 23bp wide of model fair value (114bp), and heavy issuance this year lowers the odds of more supply.
tension_points.bear_case: OAT-Bund widening toward 142bp and ongoing French budget uncertainty keep the cohort from rallying.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Progress on the French budget negotiations would remove the cap on a rally. A funding crisis in French banks would break the fair value framework.
